single.rationale: Duke Energy shows steady operating income growth (43% over 2022-2025) but faces structural headwinds including deteriorating free cash flow (-$1.7B in FY2025), rapidly escalating debt ($87.2B, up 25% since 2022), and massive capital intensity ($14B capex vs. $12.3B operating cash flow). The regulatory utility model provides stability, but execution risks around decarbonization, nuclear relicensing, environmental compliance costs, and the pending Brookfield partial sale of Duke Energy Florida create uncertainty that warrants monitoring before deeper commitment.
